contracts.label: Nullable union
contracts.detail: Merge fields by name and return null when a file does not contain an optional field. Physical types must remain compatible.

contracts.label: Exact schema
contracts.detail: Reject a dataset scan when file field names, physical types, or nullability differ from the registered contract.

changes.label: Add an optional field
changes.detail: New producers append campaign_id while old files remain unchanged.

nullable-union.headline: Old files can contribute null for campaign_id
nullable-union.explanation: The new field is optional, so a dataset reader that deliberately unions schemas can expose one campaign_id column and materialize null for files written before the change.
actions: Verify the target engines use the same schema-merge behavior.
Keep the field optional until every required historical value has been backfilled.
Track the first partition or snapshot where producers populate the field.

strict.headline: The exact schema gate rejects mixed files
strict.explanation: Both file schemas are valid Parquet, but the dataset contract requires one exact schema. Register a versioned change or rewrite old files before scanning them together.
actions: Publish a new dataset schema version before the producer rollout.
Decide whether old files are rewritten, isolated, or read through an explicit compatibility view.
Canary the new files against every strict reader.

changes.label: Rename a field
changes.detail: customer_id becomes account_id without a table-layer mapping.

nullable-union.headline: Name-based merging creates two sparse columns
nullable-union.explanation: A file-local rename does not move historical values. A name-based union sees customer_id in old files and account_id in new files unless a table format, view, or rewrite provides an explicit mapping.
actions: Add account_id while continuing to write customer_id during a transition window.
Backfill or map historical values before removing the old field.
Test filters, joins, and null counts across the transition boundary.

strict.headline: The registered field name no longer exists
strict.explanation: Strict readers resolve the expected customer_id path and fail or reject new files that only contain account_id.
actions: Stop the producer rollout until a versioned migration is approved.
Use a compatibility view or rewrite so one logical name resolves across all files.
Do not treat a rename as a metadata-only cosmetic change.

changes.label: Change a physical type
changes.detail: event_day changes from INT32 with DATE semantics to INT64.

nullable-union.headline: Null filling cannot reconcile different meanings
nullable-union.explanation: A nullable union handles missing fields, not an incompatible physical and logical type change. Engines may reject the scan or coerce values differently, so the date contract is no longer portable.
actions: Write a new field with one documented unit and logical type.
Backfill historical values with an explicit conversion.
Compare results across every production reader before cutover.

strict.headline: The physical and logical type contract changed
strict.explanation: The exact schema gate correctly rejects the new files because INT64 without DATE semantics is not the registered INT32 DATE field.
actions: Block the producer change at schema validation.
Introduce a versioned replacement field instead of mutating event_day.
Validate units, bounds, and null handling during backfill.

changes.label: Make optional data required
changes.detail: New files require customer_id even though old files can contain null.

nullable-union.headline: New enforcement does not repair historical nulls
nullable-union.explanation: The union must keep customer_id nullable while older files remain in scope. Marking only new files required changes future writes, not the facts already stored.
actions: Measure historical nulls and define a valid backfill source.
Keep the dataset-level field optional until the rewrite is complete.
Add producer validation before tightening the published contract.

strict.headline: Old and new repetition rules disagree
strict.explanation: A strict schema cannot scan the mixed files as one exact contract because customer_id is optional in one file set and required in another.
actions: Rewrite or isolate old files before registering required nullability.
Reject missing customer_id at ingestion before writing required files.
Run a full-history validation, not only a new-partition check.
